_doc: Single source of truth for per-model NPU export geometry. Consumed by tools/export_gemm_rtp.py (S2+). Geometry MUST match runtime/src/common/hub.cpp (catalog table lines 52-142 and the bfp16 adoption list lines 161-168); tools/verify_targets.py (S7) enforces parity. Mapping rules: datapath 'bfp16' -> --emulate-bfp16 --c-bf16; datapath 'bf16' -> --c-bf16 only; qkv_n null -> --qkv-n omitted (means 3*hidden); model.overrides.* beats defaults.* for that model; arches[N] supplies --cols/--batch/--batches; max_batch is a hard per-arch ceiling. datapath flag mapping lives in code (S2), not here, to avoid duplication. WHISPER (kind 'stt') adds keys the embedders do not have: heads/head_dim/enc_layers/dec_layers/mel_bins, `frames` (the model's TRUE encoder length, 1500, from max_source_positions -- the number of positions that must be computed, not the number of rows a design holds) and `max_target` (448 decoder positions). Whisper's encoder is NOT one dispatch. A shim has 16 DMA buffer descriptors and a design's live count grows with its AIE row-block count, so a single dispatch cannot exceed FOUR row-blocks: measured on npu1 with m=64/rows=4, M=256/512/1024 build and run, M=1536 and M=2048 fail to compile with \'Too many simultaneously active buffer descriptors\' and M=1536 with the derived C-path ping-pong additionally times out with ERT_CMD_STATE_TIMEOUT. 1500 rows therefore becomes 3 dispatches of 512, and `overrides.seq` is 512 -- the per-dispatch row tile, NOT frames. The runtime loops ceil(padded_frames / design.seq) times; the last chunk is padded and its extra rows are masked, which is exact because every encoder GEMM is row-independent (attention lives on the host over all 1500 positions). The padded total is 1536, i.e. 2.4% waste; a 1024-wide design would cut dispatch count to 2 at the price of 36.5% wasted arithmetic, which is the worse trade by two orders of magnitude at these sizes. The DECODER is a second design set (kinds.stt, written to gemm_rtp_dec/): its M is tokens per step, not frames, and it uses m=16 rather than 64 so its smallest M is 64 rather than 256 -- see exporters/gemm_rtp/geometry.py for why it still uses four AIE rows. Per-model `batches` exists because an STT model's unit of work is one audio file, not a batch of texts, so its tiers may be 1. tile_k 64 / tile_n 32 is forced by Whisper's geometry, not chosen: d % 64 == 0 and (d/32) % 4 == 0 for every d in {384,512,768,1024,1280}, so no operand needs padding; tile_n 48 does not divide large-v3's 5120 FFN.
